titles.title: RedAlert2
titles.engine: Westwood 2D DirectDraw engine, 16 bpp. Red Alert 2 1.006 (game.exe, md5 282f160e...) and Yuri's Revenge 1.001 (gamemd.exe, md5 03452ffd...). Both start through the Ra2.exe / RA2MD.exe stubs. The repack's gamemd.exe differs from gamemd.old in 14 small NoCD-type byte patches, and none of them touch the resolution code. The tree ships aqrit's ddraw wrapper (ddraw.dll 27,136 B + aqrit.cfg; the Vista+ launcher path swaps in _win7\aqrit.cfg).
titles.launch_sets: On a 1080p LCD with EDID (.123, .145, .195), gameplay runs at 1920x1080x16. The mechanism is present and correct: both launchers ('Launch Red Alert 2.bat', 'Launch Yuri's Revenge.bat') CALL FLEETRES.BAT and then run FLEETRES.EXE -ini "%~dp0RA2.INI" / "%~dp0RA2MD.INI" Video ScreenWidth %FR_W% and ScreenHeight %FR_H% (stage-fleetres.py:1107-1128). The agent's GAMERES rows write the same values at sync time (agent/shared/gameres.h:743-746). The staged FLEETRES.EXE md5 bb180f3b matches the repo build, and stage-fleetres --check reports it current. On all four LCD boxes the deployed ra2.ini and RA2MD.INI read ScreenWidth=1920 / ScreenHeight=1080 today. The menus and shell are a fixed 800x600 surface drawn centred, which is expected; ScreenWidth/Height only govern gameplay. Caveat: .240 has no EDID right now, so its next launch or sync falls back to the CRT rule (4:3, no larger than the persisted 1024x768) and writes 1024x768. That is a box fault, not a title fault.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver, filtered in code. Main menu -> Options (dialog 213) has a 'Set Resolution' drop-down (ctrl 1773, label GUI:SetResolution under GUI:DisplayOptions); dialog 216 has a 'Resolution Modes' list (ctrl 1497) built by the same code. The entries come from IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes, keeping only modes with dwRGBBitCount==16 and 640x480 <= mode <= max. The label format is "%d x %d x 16". The max is 4096x4096 only when [Video] AllowHiResModes=yes. Otherwise the max is 1024x768 and the width must be 640, 800 or 1024. AllowHiResModes defaults to false, and neither staged ini carries it, so today the list tops out at 1024x768 and 1920x1080 is never listed.
titles.evidence:
Disassembly of the staged binaries is in /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/rts2d-static/westwood_resolution_list_filter.txt.
game.exe, list fill at 0x542a48 (GetDlgItem 0x6ed) and 0x543d3d (GetDlgItem 0x5d9): mov al,[0xa40b41]; je -> push 0x300; push 0x400, else push 0x1000 x2; then mov edx,0x1e0; mov ecx,0x280; call 0x4962a0. Each mode is skipped when the flag is 0 and w is not 0x280/0x320/0x400.
The 0x4962a0 enumerator keeps modes where [desc+0x54] (bpp) == 16.
The constructor at 0x5d8840 sets [eax+0x29]=cl=0. Loader 0x5d8de0: Get_Bool('Video','AllowHiResModes'); that is the only xref to the key, so the game never writes it back.
gamemd.exe is identical: flag at 0xa8eb95, list code at 0x56016c and 0x56145b, constructor at 0x5fa3e1. The flag is read by absolute address only in the two list builders in each exe.
The dialog layout comes from RT_DIALOG 213/216 in game.exe.
Staged ra2.ini and RA2MD.INI [Video] contain only ScreenWidth=1024 / ScreenHeight=768 / StretchMovies=yes (no AllowHiResModes, checked case-insensitively).
Deployed copies were read today via agent DOWNLOAD: rts2d-static/deployed/{123,145,195,240}_RedAlert2_ra2.ini and _RA2MD.INI show 1920/1080 and no AllowHiResModes.
In-game screenshots show a full 1920x1080 frame: rts2d-static/ra2_123_ingame_host.png and ra2_240_ingame_joiner.png. The shell screenshot 123_RedAlert2_Launch_Red_Alert_2.png shows an 800x600 bbox centred.
titles.fix:
Add AllowHiResModes=yes under [Video] in the staged ra2.ini and RA2MD.INI. Do it the same way Tiberian Sun does:
(1) Add the key to the two staged inis.
(2) Add launcher lines "%~dp0FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%~dp0RA2.INI" Video AllowHiResModes yes, and the same for RA2MD.INI, via the stage-fleetres.py RedAlert2 recipe. The launchers already carry the FLEETRES block, so patch_launcher will not reach them; this needs a 'fix' repair pair.
(3) Add gameres.h rows { "RedAlert2", GR_OP_INI, "RA2.INI", "Video", "AllowHiResModes", "yes" } and the same for RA2MD.INI, then update the mirror and staging tests.
With this change the Options drop-down lists every 16-bpp DirectDraw mode from 640x480 up to 4096x4096, including 1920x1080. No wrapper is needed. The cnc-ddraw build on the share has inject_resolution, but an injected 1920x1080 would still be removed by the 1024x768 cap without this key.
titles.fix_source: Already in the tree: this is a stock engine key read by game.exe 1.006 at 0x5d8de0 and by gamemd.exe 1.001 at 0x5fa943. Nothing needs downloading. The legacy cnc-ddraw stack at Utility/Retro Automation/ra2-opt (docs/game-optimizations.md OPT-001) predates the staged tree and should not be mixed in.
titles.fix_risk: Low. The flag only widens the Options list: the cap rises to 4096x4096 and the width whitelist goes away; it is read nowhere else. The game never removes the key, and RA2's INIClass keeps unknown keys when it rewrites the ini on exit. A player could pick an odd mode (for example 5:4) for one session; the launcher rewrites ScreenWidth/Height to FR_W/FR_H at the next launch, so an in-game pick never persists. LAN play is unaffected, because resolution is local to each client and the WOL resolution limit (WOLLimitResolution=no, WOL only) is untouched. A 1920x1080 client sees more of the map than a 1024x768 CRT peer; that is already true today. No anti-cheat or pure-server layer is involved.
titles.hw_check:
Test on .145 or .123 (XP, where GDI can capture) and on .195 (Win7).
1. Start EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\RedAlert2" "Launch Yuri's Revenge.bat", then do the same with 'Launch Red Alert 2.bat'.
2. Press ESC twice to skip the intro. At the 800x600 shell, click Options with absolute UICLICK (proven on this shell: FINDINGS says YR was 'driven entirely with absolute UICLICK').
3. Open the 'Set Resolution' drop-down under Display Options and capture it. On XP use SCREENSHOT 0. On .195 in-game PrintScreen writes SCRN*.pcx into the game directory, since Win7 GDI returns black.
4. BEFORE the fix, expect the list to end at '1024 x 768 x 16'; that proves the diagnosis. AFTER the fix, expect a '1920 x 1080 x 16' entry. Select it, accept the keep-mode prompt, start a skirmish and confirm a 1920x1080 frame with WINLIST/SCREENSHOT.
5. Clean up with taskkill /f /im RA2MD.exe, gamemd.exe and Ra2.exe / game.exe.
titles.verifier_notes: This conclusion is derived from the binaries plus deployed configs; the drop-down has not been opened on a box yet. It also assumes each driver enumerates 1920x1080 at 16 bpp through DirectDraw. That is very likely on XP: RA2 already sets 1920x1080x16 successfully on .123/.145/.240. On Win7 WDDM (.195) it is unproven. Nothing in PER-TITLE-STATUS.md or FLEET-NOTES.txt covers the menu. Separately, .195's deployed aqrit.cfg currently reads ForceDirectDrawEmulation=1 because GAMESYNC restored the library copy; the launcher re-applies the Win7 value (0) at each launch, so this is expected.

titles.title: TiberianSun
titles.engine: Westwood 2D DirectDraw engine, 16 bpp. The exe is CnCNet-patched GAME.EXE v2.03 ('V2.03-CNCNET-PATCH- MMX ST-10', 3,739,648 B, md5 a943a851...), started via the SUN.EXE stub. There is no game-local ddraw.dll, so the system DirectDraw is used. IPXWrapper handles LAN. The CnCNet patch installs 31 jmp/call hooks into .p_text, and none of them is in the list builder (0x50b4xx) or the mode enumerator (0x4734xx).
titles.launch_sets: On a 1080p LCD with EDID, gameplay runs at 1920x1080x16. The mechanism is present and correct: 'Play Tiberian Sun.bat' CALLs FLEETRES.BAT, then FLEETRES.EXE -ini "%~dp0SUN.INI" Video ScreenWidth %FR_W%, ScreenHeight %FR_H% and AllowHiResModes yes (stage-fleetres.py:1310-1343, cap removed). The GAMERES rows at gameres.h:740-742 write the same at sync. The deployed SUN.INI on .123, .145, .195 and .240 reads 1920/1080/AllowHiResModes=yes today. An in-game frame at a true 1920x1080 was captured on .123. The menu shell is a fixed 640x400 surface drawn centred, which is expected. .240 caveat: with no EDID its next launch writes 1024x768, and its driver list currently has no 1920x1080, so neither gameplay nor the menu can reach 1080p there until the box is fixed.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver, filtered in code. Main menu -> Options (LANGUAGE.DLL dialog 213) -> Display (dialog 216 'Display Options:') -> 'Resolution Modes' listbox (ctrl 1497). The same Westwood code as RA2 fills it with DirectDraw modes whose bpp==16, labelled "%d x %d x 16". With [Video] AllowHiResModes=yes the range is 640x400 to 4096x4096 and every width is allowed. With the flag false the max is 800x600 and only widths 640 and 800 pass, which gives exactly 640x400 / 640x480 / 800x600. The staged, launcher-written and GAMERES-written SUN.INI all set yes. So 1920x1080 should be listed wherever the driver enumerates 1920x1080x16.
titles.evidence:
Disassembly is in rts2d-static/westwood_resolution_list_filter.txt.
GAME.EXE list fill at 0x50b4e9: GetDlgItem 0x5d9; mov al,[0x7e4745]; je -> push 0x258; push 0x320, else push 0x1000 x2; then mov edx,0x190; mov ecx,0x280; call 0x473400. Each mode is skipped when the flag is 0 and w is not 0x280/0x320. The mode is added with LB_ADDSTRING 0x180 and LB_SETITEMDATA 0x19a.
The 0x473400 enumerator keeps modes where [desc+0x54] == 16. The constructor at 0x589960 sets [eax+0x25]=0. Loader 0x589eb1: Get_Bool('Video','AllowHiResModes').
Staged SUN.INI: ScreenWidth=1024, ScreenHeight=768, AllowHiResModes=yes.
Deployed copies read today: rts2d-static/deployed/{123,145,195,240}_TiberianSun_SUN.INI = 1920/1080/yes.
Screenshots: rts2d-static/ts-123-skirmish-grandcanyon-1920x1080-fullscreen.png (full frame) and 123_TiberianSun_Play_Tiberian_Sun.png (640x400 shell centred).
The contrary register claim, 'its own Display Options list stops at 800x600' (PER-TITLE-STATUS.md, README-FLEETRES.md, the stage-fleetres.py:1316 comment, and the retro-3dfx FINDINGS 2026-08-30 entry), matches the AllowHiResModes=no branch exactly. Both the original 103 B staged SUN.INI and the launcher's :mkini safety net carry AllowHiResModes=no. The explanation 'CnCNet replaces hard-coded constants and bypasses the list' is not what the binary shows: the list is governed by this stock key.
titles.fix:
Nothing needed to make the list include 1920x1080; the key is already yes everywhere.
After the on-box check, correct the stale claim in PER-TITLE-STATUS.md, README-FLEETRES.md, the stage-fleetres.py comment, the test_fleetres_staging.py docstring and FINDINGS.
Optional consistency fix: change the launcher's SUN.INI safety net (the :mkini block) from AllowHiResModes=no to yes. It only fires when FLEETRES.EXE failed to write ScreenWidth, and it would then restore the 3-entry list.
titles.fix_source: Already in the tree: SUN.INI, the launcher and gameres.h all carry it. Nothing needs downloading.
titles.fix_risk: None, because nothing changes. A player's in-game pick of another mode lasts one session: the launcher rewrites ScreenWidth/Height at every launch. LAN via IPXWrapper is unaffected; resolution is local to each client.
titles.hw_check:
Test on .123 or .145 (XP), then .195.
1. Start EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\TiberianSun" "Play Tiberian Sun.bat" and press ESC past the intro.
2. At the 640x400 shell (absolute UICLICK works: FINDINGS 2026-08-31 drove Multiplayer -> Skirmish by click), go Options -> Display.
3. Capture the 'Resolution Modes' list with SCREENSHOT 0. It captured on .123 XP, and the compat DB records TS menus captured with GDI even on Win7 .246 (now .195). Expect a '1920 x 1080 x 16' entry among many.
4. Select it -> OK -> keep the mode, start a skirmish and confirm a 1920x1080 frame.
5. If the list still shows only 640x400/640x480/800x600, DOWNLOAD C:\Games\TiberianSun\SUN.INI immediately. Seeing AllowHiResModes=yes there would falsify this reading and point at the driver's 16-bpp mode list instead.
6. Clean up with taskkill /f /im GAME.EXE.
titles.verifier_notes: Static result, from disassembly plus the deployed ini; the dialog has not yet been observed with AllowHiResModes=yes. The dependency is DirectDraw enumerating 1920x1080x16. TS already sets 1920x1080x16 successfully on .123, which a DirectDraw SetDisplayMode generally requires, but this is not proven on .195 Win7 or .145. If the check fails, record it as a driver 16-bpp enumeration gap, not a TS cap.

titles.title: StarCraft
titles.engine: Blizzard Storm/DirectDraw 8-bit 2D engine, StarCraft and Brood War 1.16.1. StarCraft.exe (md5 50d53a3b...) is identical in the root and in BroodWar\. storm.dll is 1.16.1. The disc image is mounted by Daemon Tools from _disc\.
titles.launch_sets: Always 640x480x8 exclusive DirectDraw, hard-coded. The tree has no FLEETRES and none is possible. On a 1080p LCD the panel (or GPU) scaler stretches 640x480 across the whole 16:9 panel. Manual compat rows from 2026-09-01 record 'ddraw 640x480' on .145, .240 and .246 (now .195). The title does not run on .123, which has no disc mounter; the gate suppresses its shortcut there.
titles.menu_source: There is no resolution option. The only IDirectDraw::SetDisplayMode call (vtbl+0x54) in StarCraft.exe passes the immediates 640, 480, 8, and the storm.dll display init is called with 640x480.
titles.evidence:
Disassembly is in rts2d-static/fixed_mode_titles.txt.
StarCraft.exe at 0x41da3b: push 8; push 0x1e0; push 0x280; push eax; call [ecx+0x54]. This is the only 'ff 51 54' site in the exe.
At 0x41d528: push 0x10; push 0x10; push 0x1e0; push 0x280; call 0x411e2a (the storm display init). storm.dll's own SetDisplayMode at 0x15035b58 is parameterised by these arguments.
The version resource reads 1.16.1. install.reg and FLEET-NOTES.txt confirm there is no windowed mode; the only switches are ddemulate and nosound.
The compat DB row claiming '.240 verified 1920x1080' (perbox sweep, 2026-08-31) is bogus. Its screenshot, copied to rts2d-static/240_StarCraft_Play_StarCraft.png, shows the desktop with a Daemon Tools 'Unable to mount image. Unit is locked.' error, not the game.
titles.fix:
None possible: StarCraft 1.16.1 hard-codes 640x480x8 and has no video-mode setting.
The free 1.18+ patch and Remastered need Win7 x64+, Battle.net and a DX11-class GPU, and would break LAN play with the 1.16.1 peers.
A third-party injector, 'Resolution Expander' (InsectLoader + ResSettings.ini, per ModDB; a web fact), exists. It is not on the share (case-insensitive find, depth 6), is configured through an ini rather than an in-game menu, has reported campaign camera and crash bugs, and gives an unequal map view in LAN. Not recommended.
Display-only option: the cnc-ddraw 6.6.0.0 build already on the share (Utility/Retro Automation/ra2-opt/ddraw_i486.dll, subsystem 4.0) could present the 640x480 frame as a 1440x1080 pillarbox. That is untested and still does not add an in-game option.
titles.fix_source: Nothing is in the tree. The Resolution Expander would need downloading from moddb.com/games/starcraft/downloads/resolution-expander. cnc-ddraw is on the share at Utility/Retro Automation/ra2-opt/ddraw_i486.dll.
titles.fix_risk: n/a for the stock game. An injector changes game code; it can desync or crash, and a mismatched view gives an advantage in LAN. A cnc-ddraw shim adds a DLL that shadows system32, and the fleet has been bitten by game-local ddraw before (see the WarcraftII/Postal notes about Vista-only wrappers).
titles.hw_check:
This is a confirm-no-menu check on .145, .240 or .195 (boxes with Daemon Tools).
1. Start 'Play StarCraft.bat' and wait for its mount.
2. The Options menu (keyboard hotkeys plus absolute clicks) has no resolution entry.
3. During play, WINLIST or DISPLAYCFG get should show a 640x480 (8 bpp) mode.
4. For a picture, press PrintScreen; the game writes SCScrnShot_*.pcx. GDI captures of the 8-bit surface have the wrong palette.
In Brood War, do not press ESC during the intro: it quits the game.
titles.verifier_notes: The register (PER-TITLE-STATUS.md) correctly lists this title as incapable. The only defect found is the bogus 'verified 1920x1080' row for .240 in the compat DB, which should be corrected.

titles.title: WarcraftII
titles.engine: Blizzard 8-bit DirectDraw 2D engine, sharing the 'GDS vidinimo' display code with StarCraft. This is GOG's Warcraft II Battle.net Edition 2.02b: 'Warcraft II BNE.exe', md5 c158c81d..., subsystem 4.0. GOG's _dx build and its Vista-only ddraw.dll are deliberately not staged.
titles.launch_sets: Always 640x480x8 exclusive DirectDraw, hard-coded. The tree has no FLEETRES and none is possible. On a 1080p LCD the panel scaler stretches the image to fill. The compat DB records 'ddraw 640x480' on .123, .240 and .246.
titles.menu_source: There is no resolution option. The only SetDisplayMode call passes the immediates 640, 480, 8.
titles.evidence:
From rts2d-static/fixed_mode_titles.txt: 'Warcraft II BNE.exe' at 0x48c489: push 8; push 0x1e0; push 0x280; ... call [ecx+0x54] (0x48c498). This is the only such site, and the _dx exe has the same bytes at the same offset.
requires.json says 'a fixed 640x480, no per-box resolution to write'. launch.txt documents why the _dx build and GOG's ddraw.dll are not staged: the wrapper is SubsystemVersion 6.0, and XP refuses it.
Every GDI screenshot in the perbox sweep is all-black 640x480, because the 8-bit surface cannot be captured.
titles.fix:
None possible within BNE 2.02b: the mode is hard-coded and there is no video menu.
Display-only alternative: the cnc-ddraw 6.6.0.0 i486 build on the share (subsystem 4.0, XP-loadable) could upscale to a 1440x1080 pillarbox. That is untested and adds no in-game option.
Wargus (Stratagus) has a resolution menu, but it is a different engine: not on the share, a separate data extraction, and LAN-incompatible with BNE. It does not qualify as a fix.
titles.fix_source: Nothing is in the tree. cnc-ddraw is on the share at Utility/Retro Automation/ra2-opt/ddraw_i486.dll. Wargus would need downloading from github.com/Wargus/wargus.
titles.fix_risk: n/a for the stock game. A game-local ddraw.dll shadows system32 on every box that syncs it, and the GOG Vista-only wrapper shows that failure mode on XP. IPXWrapper LAN would be unaffected by a display shim.
titles.hw_check:
This is a confirm-no-menu check.
1. Start EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\WarcraftII" "Play Warcraft II.bat".
2. In the in-game menu (F10 -> Options: Sound / Speeds / Preferences) there is no resolution option.
3. During play, WINLIST or DISPLAYCFG get should read 640x480 (8 bpp).
4. GDI cannot capture the 8-bit surface, so use a photo or PrintScreen if the game supports it.
5. Clean up with taskkill /f /im "Warcraft II BNE.exe".
titles.verifier_notes: PER-TITLE-STATUS.md has no row for this title (checked case-insensitively); add one with the 'incapable, fixed 640x480x8' measurement.

titles.title: WarcraftOrcsAndHumans
titles.engine: DOS WAR.EXE (DOS4GW LE, GOG 1.2) in VGA mode 13h (320x200x256), running under GOG's DOSBox 0.74-2.1. That DOSBox.exe (md5 2318a446...) is the same binary Daggerfall and MOO2 ship.
titles.launch_sets: The result on the 1080p LCDs is wrong today: the game appears as a small, unscaled 640x480 box centred in a black 1920x1080 screen. All three launchers run FLEETRES.EXE -ini dosboxWC1.conf sdl fullresolution %FR_DOSFULLRES%, which gives 'desktop' on an LCD with EDID; GAMERES row gameres.h:799 writes the same. So DOSBox takes the 1920x1080 desktop mode, but the base conf sets output=surface, and DOSBox 0.74 cannot scale in surface mode; with a fixed fullresolution it just centres the 320x200 -> normal2x + aspect -> 640x480 image. The deployed dosboxWC1.conf on .123, .145, .195 and .240 reads fullresolution=desktop plus output=surface. On .240 today (no EDID) the value flips to 'original', so the desktop switches to 640x480 and the LCD stretches it.
titles.menu_source: There is no resolution option in the game. It is a 1994 320x200 VGA title: WAR.EXE sets mode 13h and never uses VESA 4F02h. Only DOSBox's own [sdl] output settings decide how it fills the panel.
titles.evidence:
Evidence files:
- rts2d-static/dosbox_output_surface.txt
- rts2d-static/fixed_mode_titles.txt
WAR.EXE has 'mov eax,13h; int 10h' at file offset 0x3474f and no b8024f0000 / 66b8024f anywhere.
The staged DOSBox.exe's own help text reads 'If you end up with small window on a large screen, try an output different from surface.'
Screenshots rts2d-static/{123,240,246}_WarcraftOrcsAndHumans_*.png are 1920x1080 frames with the content bbox at (640,367)-(1280,712), i.e. an unscaled box. The .124 CRT shot fills its 640x480 frame.
Controls on the same LCD boxes: Descent1 (output=ddraw) and RedneckRampage (output=overlay) fill (240,0)-(1680,1080), a 1440x1080 pillarbox; see 123_Descent1_Play_Descent.png and 123_RedneckRampage_*.png.
Deployed confs: rts2d-static/deployed/*_WarcraftOrcsAndHumans_dosboxWC1.conf.
The compat DB rows 'dosbox 1920x1080 verified' for .123/.240/.246 describe the DOSBox mode, not the picture, and are misleading.
requires.json's note '640x480 VGA' is wrong: the game is 320x200.
titles.fix:
No in-game option can exist. The display fix is a one-word change in the staged dosboxWC1.conf [sdl]: output=surface becomes output=overlay. Four of the other five staged DOSBox titles use overlay, including Daggerfall on the identical DOSBox.exe; output=ddraw (as Descent1 uses) is the fallback.
Keep fullresolution per box (FLEETRES and GAMERES already handle it) and keep aspect=true.
Result: 'desktop' shows a 1440x1080 4:3 pillarbox on the LCDs, and CRT boxes keep 'original'.
Then purge and GAMESYNC the title per the staged-game loop.
titles.fix_source: Already in the tree: a DOSBox 0.74-2.1 conf key. The same DOSBox build runs Daggerfall with output=overlay.
titles.fix_risk: Low. The change affects the local display path only; IPXNET LAN and the game itself are untouched. Overlay on Win7 WDDM is the one variable, but ShadowWarrior's overlay rendered 1728x1080 on .246 (now .195) in the perbox sweep, and Descent1's ddraw rendered 1440x1080 there. Verify on .195 and one XP LCD, and fall back to ddraw if overlay misbehaves.
titles.hw_check:
1. After the conf change, start EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\WarcraftOrcsAndHumans" "Play Warcraft - Orcs and Humans.bat" on .145 or .123 (XP; this DOSBox surface is GDI-capturable).
2. Wait about 20 s and take SCREENSHOT 0. Measure the content bbox: expect about (240,0)-(1680,1080) instead of (640,367)-(1280,712).
3. Repeat on .195 (Win7). GDI may be black there; if so, rely on the DOSBox window rect via WINLIST.
4. There is no in-game menu to check; the campaign and network screens are mouse-only per the compat notes.
5. Clean up with taskkill /f /im DOSBox.exe.
titles.verifier_notes: This is a real defect the task did not anticipate: the fleet records 'verified fullscreen 1920x1080' while the picture uses about a third of the panel width. PER-TITLE-STATUS.md has no row for this title; add one. .240's lost EDID turns this title into a desktop mode switch, which is a separate box fault.

titles.title: MasterOfOrionII
titles.engine: DOS ORION2.EXE (DOS/16M) carrying the unofficial 1.40 beta patch ('Ver 1.40b23') on 1.31 data. It runs 640x480x8 through VESA, under GOG's DOSBox 0.74-2.1 (the same DOSBox.exe md5 2318a446 as WC1). ORION95.EXE (Win32 1.31) is staged only as the icon source.
titles.launch_sets: Same defect as WC1: on the 1080p LCDs the 640x480 VESA image sits unscaled in the middle of a black 1920x1080 screen. The three launchers run FLEETRES.EXE -ini dosboxMOO2.conf sdl fullresolution %FR_DOSFULLRES% ('desktop' on an LCD), and GAMERES row gameres.h:796 writes the same. But the base conf's output=surface cannot scale, so DOSBox centres the 640x480 frame. The deployed dosboxMOO2.conf on .123, .145, .195 and .240 reads fullresolution=desktop plus output=surface. On .240 today (no EDID) the value flips to 'original', a 640x480 desktop mode that the LCD stretches.
titles.menu_source: There is no resolution option. ORION2.EXE's video path is a fixed VESA 640x480 (Test_For_Vesa / Set_Video_Mode_Vesa). The exe and ESTRINGS.LBX carry no user-facing resolution, video or hi-res strings. The unofficial 1.50 patch also adds no hi-res mode (web sources: GOG and Steam forum threads). How it fills the panel is purely DOSBox's [sdl] output.
titles.evidence:
Evidence files:
- rts2d-static/dosbox_output_surface.txt
- rts2d-static/fixed_mode_titles.txt
ORION2.EXE strings include 'Ver 1.40b23', 'You must run VESA.COM.' and Set_Video_Mode_Vesa.
Screenshots rts2d-static/{123,240,246}_MasterOfOrionII_Play_Master_of_Orion_II.png are 1920x1080 frames with the content bbox at (720,460)-(1200,620). The .124 CRT shot shows the same intro content at (80,160)-(560,320), so on the LCD the 640x480 frame sits at offset (640,300), unscaled.
Deployed confs: rts2d-static/deployed/*_MasterOfOrionII_dosboxMOO2.conf.
The staged conf sets output=surface, aspect=true, scaler=normal2x. Since 640x480 is not a doubled mode, normal2x does not apply either.

titles.title: Postal
titles.engine: Running With Scissors' SDL2 rebuild ('POSTAL Classic and Uncut', GOG). Postal.exe is dated 2018-05-21 and ships with SDL2.dll. It needs SSE2, which all four LCD boxes have (Athlon 64 or i5-2400). It renders an 8-bit frame through SDL_Renderer with a linear scale hint.
titles.launch_sets:
On a 1080p LCD this build takes the desktop mode by itself: a fullscreen-desktop window at 1920x1080 with no mode switch. The game world renders to a logical frame of 480 lines times the desktop aspect, 853x480 at 16:9, which SDL scales to fill the panel with no bars. 'Play Postal.bat' CALLs FLEETRES.BAT but writes nothing and passes no arguments, which is correct.
Mechanism, from the binary: with no -resolution or -windowed argument, Disp_Init leaves the requested size at 0x0, so rspSetVideoMode creates the window with flags 0x1001 (SDL_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN_DESKTOP). The mode list is a single entry, SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode(0). SetupVideo sets the display width to desk_w*480/desk_h when the desktop is larger than 640x480. POSTAL.INI [Video] DeviceWidth/DeviceHeight/UseCurrentDeviceDimensions (staged as UseCurrentDeviceDimensions=0) do not size the window in this build.
The title is deployed on .123, .145, .195 and .240 but has never been launched there: no %APPDATA%\RunningWithScissors exists on .145, .123 or .195. All of the above is derived from the binary, not observed.
titles.menu_source: There is no resolution option: OPTIONS -> VIDEO contains only GAMMA. Both the exe's menu string table and the game's own Help/play/menus.htm ('VIDEO MENU: GAMMA') show this. A '-resolution WxH' command-line switch exists, but it only picks a real fullscreen mode for the window; it does not change the 480-line internal render.
titles.evidence:
From rts2d-static/fixed_mode_titles.txt:
- Disp_Init at 0x42f4e0: rspCommandLine('resolution') then sscanf '%dx%d' into [0x537018]/[0x53701c]; else 'windowed' sets 1024x768; else 0x0.
- rspSetVideoMode at 0x42fd0a..0x42fd1b: flags 1 if a size was requested, else 0x1001. It then calls SDL_CreateWindow (0x42fd51) and SDL_RenderSetLogicalSize with the display area (0x42fe5e).
- 0x42fa30 builds the mode list with SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode, falling back to 640x480.
- SetupVideo at 0x423233: if h>480 && w>640, width = w*480/h.
- INI defaults at 0x4234e1: DeviceWidth 640, DeviceHeight 480, UseCurrentDeviceDimensions 1.
- Menu strings: OPTIONS / VIDEO / GAMMA.
The deployed POSTAL.INI on the four LCD boxes is identical to the staged copy (rts2d-static/deployed/*_Postal_POSTAL.INI).
rts2d-static/readonly_checks.txt holds the %APPDATA% listings of the parent folders (no RunningWithScissors, checked case-insensitively).
titles.fix: None needed: the build already fills a 1920x1080 panel with a widescreen 853x480 logical frame. None is possible for an in-game 1080p option, because the engine renders at a fixed 480-line height and exposes no video-size menu; adding one would mean modifying the code.
titles.fix_risk: n/a. Postal multiplayer is unaffected either way, since resolution is local. Possible trap: the exe resolves files through a per-user folder (FindCorrectFile at 0x43ce4f: SHGetFolderPath with CSIDL_APPDATA|CREATE plus \RunningWithScissors\Postal Plus\), so a per-user POSTAL.INI may shadow the staged one after first run. That is harmless here because the ini does not size the window.

titles.verifier_notes: UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE, as requires.json already says. The claims here come from disassembly. PER-TITLE-STATUS.md has no row for this title. If the title comes up at 640x480, the likely cause is a desktop left at 640x480 by an earlier game: SetupVideo then falls back to the 4:3 DeviceWidth/Height, and FULLSCREEN_DESKTOP inherits the live mode.
